**GoCardless processes first agentic account-to-account payment in the UK**

*The transaction marks a milestone for account-to-account rails in the emerging agentic payments category, where most early activity has run over card networks.*

GoCardless has completed what it describes as the first agentic account-to-account payment in the UK, processing an AI-driven charitable donation to the anti-poverty charity Trussell. The transaction was initiated and executed by an AI agent on the GoCardless website without manual human intervention at the point of payment.

Agentic payments, where AI systems autonomously initiate and complete transactions on behalf of users, have been gathering momentum across Europe since early 2026. Until now, the category has been dominated by card-based implementations. Mastercard, Visa and several European banks have run agentic pilots using card credentials, and EMVCo has drafted a framework specifically for card-based agentic transactions. GoCardless's move extends the concept to bank-to-bank rails, opening a parallel track that could prove significant for recurring and subscription payments where card-on-file has traditionally dominated.

GoCardless, which was among the founding providers on the UK Payments Initiative when it went live on June 2 and reported its first profitable quarter in April, continues to position itself at the intersection of open banking infrastructure and emerging payment categories. Whether agentic account-to-account payments gain traction beyond demonstration use cases will depend on the development of consent frameworks and liability models that are still largely unresolved.

*Sources: [GoCardless processes the first agentic account-to-account payment in the UK](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/gocardless-processes-the-first-agentic-account-to-account-payment-in-the-uk/) — Openbankingexpo | [GoCardless processes first agentic account-to-account transaction in the UK](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110969/gocardless-processes-first-agentic-account-to-account-transaction-in-the-uk?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Airtel Money files for London IPO at up to $9bn valuation**

*A listing that could value the mobile payments business at up to $9 billion would test whether London can still attract high-growth fintechs after a string of departures to New York.*

Airtel Money, the mobile payments arm of Airtel Africa, is preparing to file for a London initial public offering that could raise at least $800 million and value the business at up to $9 billion. The listing would separate the payments business from its parent and give it direct access to public capital markets.

The IPO arrives at a sensitive moment for the London Stock Exchange, which has seen a succession of fintechs either move their primary listing to the US or choose New York over London for new offerings. Wise confirmed plans to shift its primary listing to the US in April. A successful Airtel Money debut would be a counterpoint, though the logic is different: Airtel Money's core operations are across sub-Saharan Africa, and London has traditionally been a stronger listing venue for companies with African and emerging-market exposure than US exchanges.

Airtel Money processes mobile payments across 14 African markets and has been growing transaction volumes rapidly as mobile money adoption deepens across the continent. The business sits at the intersection of mobile telecoms and payments infrastructure in markets where traditional banking penetration remains low.

*Sources: [Airtel Money to launch London IPO](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48457/airtel-money-to-launch-london-ipo?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Russian fintech A7 funnelled billions in sanctioned payments through global banks**

*A Financial Times investigation reveals how a Kremlin-controlled fintech exploited weaknesses in bank compliance controls to process sanctions-busting payments for Russian state companies.*

A7, a Russian fintech with ties to the Kremlin, tricked international banks into handling billions of dollars in payments to Russian state companies subject to Western sanctions, according to an investigation by the Financial Times. The scheme exploited gaps in bank compliance controls, routing payments through intermediaries in ways that obscured their ultimate origin and destination.

The scale of the operation raises pointed questions about the effectiveness of sanctions enforcement in the payments chain. Banks have invested heavily in sanctions screening since 2022, and regulators across Europe and the US have repeatedly tightened expectations around correspondent banking due diligence. The A7 case suggests that a determined, state-backed actor can still find systematic vulnerabilities, particularly where fintech intermediaries sit between sanctioned entities and the global banking system.

The investigation is likely to intensify regulatory scrutiny of fintech counterparties and the adequacy of know-your-customer procedures applied to payment facilitators operating in or adjacent to sanctioned jurisdictions. The European Banking Authority and national regulators have already been pressing for stronger anti-money-laundering controls as instant payment volumes grow.

*Sources: [Russian fintech A7 exploited bank controls to funnel billion of dollars in sanctioned payments](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48446/russian-fintech-a7-exploited-bank-controls-to-funnel-billion-of-dollars-in-sanctioned-payments?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Tink founders launch AI compliance startup after $2bn exit**

*Daniel Kjellen and Fredrik Hedberg, whose open banking platform Tink was acquired by Visa in 2022, have emerged from stealth with Freda, an AI-native compliance startup.*

Daniel Kjellen and Fredrik Hedberg, co-founders of the open banking platform Tink, have launched Freda, a bootstrapped AI-native compliance startup that has been operating in stealth. Tink was acquired by Visa for $1.9 billion in 2022 and now forms part of Visa's open banking infrastructure.

Freda's focus on compliance reflects a growing recognition that regulatory obligations, particularly around anti-money-laundering, fraud prevention and transaction monitoring, represent one of the most acute operational pain points for banks and payment providers. The founders chose to bootstrap rather than raise venture capital, an unusual approach at a time when many AI startups are raising large rounds, suggesting either a deliberate constraint on growth pace or confidence in reaching revenue quickly.

Several successful European fintech founders have returned to build in adjacent categories. Kjellen and Hedberg appear to see AI-driven compliance tooling as an underdeveloped market with significant demand from the institutions they previously served as infrastructure providers.

*Sources: [From one of Europe's biggest fintech exits to bootstrapping an AI startup: 'There's no limitation'](https://sifted.eu/articles/tink-founders-launch-freda) — Sifted*

**ACI Worldwide connects cloud payments hub to Swift's shared ledger**

*Intelligent routing for Swift ledger transactions is now available through ACI's cloud-native platform, extending practical access to tokenised settlement infrastructure beyond the largest banks.*

ACI Worldwide is integrating Swift's shared ledger into ACI Connetic, its cloud-native payments hub, enabling intelligent routing for transactions on the ledger. The move gives ACI's bank clients a path to access Swift's tokenised settlement rails without building direct integrations themselves.

The integration extends access beyond the handful of large institutions participating directly in Swift's pilots to the broader universe of mid-tier and regional banks that rely on vendor platforms for their payments processing. ACI's client base spans more than 80 countries. Swift's shared ledger has been progressing from prototype to pilot since BNP Paribas and HSBC completed the first corporate payment on it in September.

Infrastructure vendors are positioning themselves as the connective layer between legacy payment systems and emerging tokenised settlement rails. ACI agreed to acquire Cranium Ventures on September 1 for cloud-native card switching, with the deal expected to close in the third quarter, and the Swift integration continues the theme of building out Connetic as a multi-rail hub.

*Sources: [ACI Worldwide connects with Swift's ledger](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110976/aci-worldwide-connects-with-swifts-ledger?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
